messages:
Elaine: FYI got a high-severity from payments team — customers hitting 429s during lunch ramp. They see bursts for a few minutes then quota exhaustion and continued 429s. Asking if our defaults for RPM/TPM + burst are sane, and wants repro steps so Support can triage.

Raj: Can reproduce in staging quickly. Looks like two things: per-key token-bucket limit (RPM/TPM) and the short burst window that allows ~2x allowance then drops to sustained rate. I'll post a minimal k6 script I used.

Mike: Sharing numbers from my run earlier today (staging, dedicated small pool):
- steady target: 100rpm per key -> stable
- burst ramp: 500rpm for 60s -> immediate 429 spike after ~75s
- 429s had Retry-After sometimes, sometimes absent (race when quota metadata not populated fast enough)
- 95p latency jumped from 120ms -> 900ms during bursts
- token consumption showed cumulative tokens depleted, refill rate matched TPM setting

Raj: k6 snippet (pasteable):

```
import http from 'k6/http';
import { sleep } from 'k6';
export default function () {
  let res = http.post('https://staging.redwood/api/v1/generate', JSON.stringify({prompt: 'hi'}), {
    headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer ${API_KEY}', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }
  });
  sleep(0.1); // ~600rpm per virtual user
}
```

Run with: `k6 run --vus 10 --duration 2m script.js` then increase vus to ramp bursts.

Lucy: Important to include the model weight in our calculations — long completions eat TPM quickly. For tests, use a short prompt and limit tokens to 64. Also set header `X-Client-Id` to simulate different API keys (we throttle per key + per-project policies).

Elaine: Support asked for exact repro steps to attach to the ticket. Can we make a 1-page checklist they can run in a pinch?

Raj: Draft quick checklist:
1) Get a staging API key (team:support-staging)
2) Use k6 script above, set prompt tokens <=64
3) Baseline: run steady 100rpm for 3m, capture 200/429 counts and latency
4) Burst test: do 5x target for 60s then drop back to baseline for 5m
5) Capture headers: `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `Retry-After` and server logs on quota decisions
6) If 429s persist after burst window, collect server-side token-bucket logs (ask eng-runtime for trace id)

Mike: I ran a variant that also hit the on-request routing fallback: when a model variant was evicted under load, requests were rerouted to smaller model and latency increased but 429s reduced. Good fallback behavior, but product owners might not want silent model fallback.

Lucy: Proposed sane defaults (early recommendation):
- per-key RPM: 120
- per-key TPM: 900
- burst multiplier: 2.5x for 60s window
- sustained enforcement: apply strict per-minute refill after burst
Rationale: lets short interactive spikes pass but prevents long sustained abuse.

SRE-Bot: NOTE: rate-limit policy change requires config rollout to staging -> canary -> prod. Use feature flag `rl_policy_v2`.

Elaine: Can we schedule an automated load-run in staging every weekday at 10:30 for 30m and push results to the ops dashboard? That would help spot regressions when we change kernel/quant.

Raj: I'll set up a GitHub Actions job + k6 that pushes metrics to Grafana. Need a service account key. ETA: EOD tomorrow.

Support-Bot: Ticket #INC-4721 linked. Customer provided timestamps and sample request ids: req_zt9x, req_zt9y. Attaching after you run the repro will help correlate logs.

Mike: A few gotchas I hit:
- If you hammer with many distinct API keys, project-level quotas kick in faster than per-key ones. Run single-key tests to validate per-key behavior.
- If you sleep too little in k6 (0.01s) you produce CPU-bound noise on client side, not network-bound. Keep realistic pacing.

Lucy: Also verify billing-metering edgecases: token accounting was slightly delayed during bursts; make sure billing pipeline deduplicates and uses authoritative per-request token dump.

Elaine: Action items:
- Raj: produce one-click k6 script + checklist and upload to /ops/playbooks by tomorrow
- Raj: wire automated staging job + Grafana push (EOD tomorrow)
- Mike: run model-fallback scenario and attach logs to INC-4721
- Lucy: propose final default numbers and write a short RFC for product (due end of week)

Raj: Got it. I'll post the script and a short runbook here when done. @Elaine ping me if Support needs a walkthrough :thumbsup:

Mike: tagging runtime team for Retry-After inconsistencies: @runtime-team please confirm header consistency.

SRE-Bot: Deploy job created: `rl-policy-canary` (status: queued)

Elaine: Thanks all — this looks actionable. We'll update the customer once we have a reproducible trace and can recommend configuration changes or ask them to adopt exponential backoff on client side.
